releases.summary: Cue list fixes: the step box keeps its cue selected, Paste goes above the selection, and what's typed in the Inspector shows in the list as it's typed.

changes.text: Paste puts the copies above the selected cue (with End of List selected, at the end).
After a Delete, the cue above the one deleted is selected.
What's typed in the Inspector's Number, Name, Page, Department and Notes shows in the cue list as it's typed. It's stored (one undo) on Enter, Tab or leaving the box.
Clicking a cue in the list after typing in the Inspector gives the keys back to the list.
Opening or closing a step with its box could select a different cue. The step's own cue is now selected.
Typing in the Inspector and then clicking another cue could lose what was typed. It's now stored on the cue it was typed for.
Windows: dragging the cue list's scroll bar stopped when the pointer moved off the bar. The drag now follows the pointer until the button comes up.

releases.summary: Space out a repeated sound with a Tail, an SFX 6-style bus grid on the Patch page, a collapsible Inspector, and windows that open on screen.

changes.text: Time tab: a Tail column for the whole cue and for each loop: seconds of silence after each pass, so a chime played several times can be spaced out.
Patch page: one grid of busses (name, Gain and Group) against the sound card's outputs, as in SFX 6. Add, delete and move busses; a bus keeps its patch when it moves.
Name the sound card's outputs (FOH L, Sub…) on each computer, and choose in Preferences the group new cues play on.
Windows ▸ Inspector ▸ Collapsed: the Inspector shrinks to its title bar; click it to open it to fit what's in it. Preferences can have GO close it again.
A sound cue's busses are set in its matrix (Levels); the Inspector no longer asks for an Output.
Scrubbing a playing cue in the Master Transport keeps the levels of Fades below it that have already run.
The cue list's transport buttons light up as they're pressed.
Wait and Autofollow effects no longer have a Triggers tab: they link the effects around them.

Windows: with screens at different scales, windows could open partly off the screen, or draw their contents too large until resized. They now open where they were left, on a screen, and maximized windows come back maximized.

releases.summary: The cue list scrolls while you drag, always shows its scroll bar and keeps the active cue in view, and fixes for Mac crashes on dropdowns and text boxes.

changes.text: Dragging an effect, a file or a cue near the top or bottom of the cue list scrolls the list.
The cue list's scroll bar is always shown: click above or below the thumb to move a page, or drag the thumb.
The standby cue and the selected cue are scrolled into view when they change, so the arrow keys, Prev/Next and GO always keep them on screen.
A cue dragged to a new place in the list is selected when it's dropped.
Mac: clicking a dropdown (the Patch page's sound card or buffer, a Command effect's command, and others) closed SFX 7. Dropdowns now open as a Mac menu.
Mac: SFX 7 could close when a cue's details refreshed while the cursor was in one of its text boxes.

releases.summary: Drop effects and files below End of List, Fades and Stops that find their cue, and fixes for dragging from the Finder and for starting the engine.

changes.text: Effects from the Effect List, and audio and video files, can be dropped in the empty space below End of List: they go just above End of List.
A Fade or Stop dropped in with no cue selected to act on targets the nearest Audio, Video or Live Audio cue above where it lands.
Windows: the engine failed to start ("Engine Failed", "did not accept connections within 10s") when the Windows user name has letters like é, as in José.
Mac: audio and video files dragged in from the Finder now drop into the cue list (they were ignored).
Mac: dragging a file from the Finder over the cue list could close SFX 7.

releases.summary: SFX 7 asks for a license as it opens, GO! with the standby cue's notes beside it, and clearer quit questions.

changes.text: With no license that runs on this computer (none yet, or a trial or rental that has ended), the License window opens as SFX 7 starts. Activate a key, start a free trial or add weeks there and SFX 7 opens; otherwise Quit SFX 7 closes it.
A trial or rental that ends while SFX 7 is open never stops the show: it keeps running until you quit.
GO is now GO!, and the standby cue's notes sit in a shaded box beside it.
A cue's Notes (Properties) take several lines, three in view.
Join codes and license keys are typed in capitals, with their dashes put in.
Quitting asks with stacked buttons: Save, Don't Save or Cancel, then Stop the Engine and Quit (press Enter), Keep the Engine Running and Quit, or Cancel.
Play mode also hides Network, Diagnostics, and File > License and License Agreement.
The Play buttons and the Master Transport no longer play cues without a license.
Closing a panel's own window could make SFX 7 report an error later, for example when clicking into a cue's Name.
Windows: File > About shows the right version number (it said 1.0.0.1).

releases.summary: A larger, sharper look on the Mac, and a fix for the Master Transport.

changes.text: Clicking around in a playing cue's waveform in the Master Transport no longer drops the cue from the transport and the cue list's playing indicator while it keeps playing.
Mac: SFX 7 is drawn at the Mac's own size, so text and controls are about 30% larger, as in other Mac apps.
Mac: SFX 7 > Settings... (Command-comma) opens Preferences.
Mac: Media, Remote, History, Network, Preferences and Diagnostics no longer show a back arrow that led to a list with no way back to the show.

releases.summary: The license agreement, a clearer way to quit, and fixes for the Mac.

changes.text: The license agreement is shown the first time SFX 7 opens (and on the Windows installer's license page), and any time in File > License Agreement.
Quitting asks whether to save the show first, then whether to stop the show engine.
The main window opens on most of the screen the first time and remembers where it was. In a narrow window, the side panels move under the cue list as tabs.
The docked Master Transport shows beside the cue list. A long cue name could leave it no room.
License keys pasted with extra spaces or other dash characters are accepted.
Mac: shows open in the downloaded app, and Quit finishes the first time.

releases.summary: The first release of SFX 7: sound, video and show control for theatre and live events, on Windows and Mac.

changes.text: One cue list, one GO: sound, video and show-control cues with waits, autofollows, fades and the Master Transport.
Design mode to build the show and Play mode to run it.
Patch your sound card's outputs into busses, with a matrix, and play live inputs in Live Audio cues.
Fire cues from a lighting desk, show controller or button box with OSC, MIDI and MIDI Show Control.
Panels can be docked or opened in their own windows, on Windows and Mac (Apple silicon and Intel).
Free 7-day trial, weekly rental or purchase. Activation needs the internet once, then SFX 7 runs offline.
